answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost. A opal stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a vine...
